{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"8e1f26f9f857254c9e405b26962101d5020780e1f110c49a281e69dc1b9c0396","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:100","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Alcohol and Other Drugs","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Alcohol and Other Drugs","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Alcohol and Other Drugs

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A02
A blood alcohol content above point zero five but below point zero eight makes a driver impaired, while point zero eight or more makes the driver under the influence [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint thresholds; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F14 and sec11-F10.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
The adult threshold for administrative revocation is point zero eight [A01], while the zero tolerance threshold for drivers under twenty-one is point zero two [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint thresholds; prereq_hint sec11-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F11 and sec11-F10.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A02
A failed test and a refused test both trigger administrative revocation with a thirty-day temporary permit [A01], while refusal adds a one, two or four year revocation based on prior alcohol enforcement contacts [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint consent-and-refusal; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F10 and sec11-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
Alcohol depresses reflexes, judgment, alertness and vision, while the stimulated feeling after drinking is only the loss of inhibition [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint effects; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec11-F04 and sec11-F02.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
Food eaten before drinking slows how fast alcohol acts, while food, coffee or a cold shower taken afterward does nothing to remove alcohol already in the blood [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint effects; prereq_hint sec11-R04; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F06 and sec11-F07.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
Consuming or possessing alcohol on a public highway or sidewalk is illegal, while keeping an opened container in the passenger area of a vehicle is a separate prohibition on public roads [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint open-container; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec11-F15 and sec11-F16.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A02
Prescription and over-the-counter medicines such as allergy and cold pills can impair driving, while illegal drugs such as LSD, heroin and cocaine can leave a user unaware of the surroundings altogether [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint drugs; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec11-F18 and sec11-F21.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
Amphetamines are stimulants sold illegally as pep pills and speed, while tranquilizers and sedatives are downers, and an overdose of either can be fatal on its own [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint drugs; prereq_hint sec11-R07; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F19 and sec11-F20.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A01
Implied consent means every driver has already agreed to be tested, while administrative revocation is what follows when the test is failed or refused [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint consent-and-refusal; prereq_hint sec11-R03; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec11-F09 and sec11-F10.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A02
A test can convict a driver by showing alcohol, while it can also clear a driver by showing none, and refusing it does not prevent a driving under the influence charge [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint consent-and-refusal; prereq_hint sec11-R09; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec11-F13 and sec11-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0056]
